cd /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering && ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q  ->  809 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed in 127.18s. HEAD (b12dca2) collected 806 and was 795 passed / 10 skipped / 1 xfailed, so this is +14 tests and zero failures; skipped and xfailed counts unchanged. tests/test_generator_hooks.py alone: 41 passed in 1.16s (was 27).

Every fix was additionally checked by reverting it in the working tree and re-running the file (harness /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/wp5_fix/mutate.py, which restores the working-tree text rather than git-checking-out): defect 1's revert fails 1 test, defect 2's two reverts (plain sum / full-count denominator) fail 4 and 4, defect 3's revert fails 2. Before the fixes all four reverts left 27/27 green.
deviations: hook_rng (defect 3) no longer uses the design's literal `random.Random((seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF)`. New module function `_hook_seed(seed, rng)` returns `f"alphacube.hook_rng/{rng.getstate()[1]!r}"` when the rng exposes state, and falls back to the design's formula otherwise (SystemRandom / duck-typed rngs raise on getstate). Reason: the literal formula cannot satisfy either property it is documented for at the only in-tree construction site. I did NOT take the reviewer's second option (keep the formula, add `seed=seed` at gp.py:241) because gp.py is WP7's owned file; WP7's step 2 still needs no change under this fix, but if the coordinator prefers the literal formula then WP7 must add `seed=seed` there and `_hook_seed` should be reverted. Deviation is stated in `_hook_seed`'s docstring and in the test module's docstring.

Defect 2's suggested `_pick_weighted` body was adopted in substance but not verbatim: I build `live_specs` with a loop instead of a dict comprehension plus a separate `live` list, so a face is dropped by having no surviving entry rather than by a second pass. Same two `choices` draws, same order; verified draw-for-draw against a local copy of Partura's `pick` over five weight regimes.

Defect 1's suggested ban-set enumeration (`for _ in range(400): keys |= one_layer_keys(probe._collapse_leaf(s))`) would make the `len(keys) == 320` assertion flaky: 2 of the 26 root reducers are binary, i.e. 64 ordered field pairs each, and 400 samples miss one with ~20% probability. The test helper `_reachable_minimal_keys` enumerates `itertools.product(gen.fields, repeat=n)` exhaustively instead; verified to give the identical 320-key set as 2000 samples per spec.

Defect 2's suggested test (1) — '`op_weight=lambda s: 1.0` must give the same face-share distribution as `op_weight=None` over ~100k draws' — is implemented as a deterministic assertion plus a small sampled one rather than 100k draws, to keep the file at ~1.2s: a `_ChoicesRecorder` rng reads the face masses straight off the `choices` call and asserts they are all equal, and the sampled check runs 4000 draws over a deliberately lopsided 12-spec, 2-face slice (10 dt vs 2 nd) where the broken versions give 0.833 and 0.091 against the correct 0.5. Both mutations die.
No files outside the WP5 package were touched. gp.py:241 still passes `rng=` and no `seed=`; that is now harmless but is the line a reviewer of WP7 should look at.

Added one explanatory comment inside `generate()`'s fallback (owned file) marking the `_ban_ok` conjunct as load-bearing and naming the test that pins it, so the leak cannot be reintroduced by a refactor that reads only the code.

Scratch: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/wp5_fix/ (mutate.py, probe_pick.py, probe_hook_rng.py, probe_fallback.py, probe_shapes.py, probe_partura_parity.py, probe_stream_identity.py). Nothing outside the two owned files in the worktree was modified; /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube is still clean at 517fd09; no push, no ssh.

DEFECT 1 — vacuous fallback test (high) — REPRODUCED, FIXED.
Reproduction: deleting `self._ban_ok(tree) and` from generator.py:248 left 27/27 green, exactly as reported. Measured why: 320 minimal keys are reachable from `_collapse_leaf` over the 26 root reducers and 8 fields, the old test banned 1, so the first fallback draw hits the victim 0.31% of the time; with seed 2 the un-guarded version returns `day_durbin_watson(Ret)`, which satisfies both of the old assertions. Confirmed the check is load-bearing exactly as the report says: banning 319 of the 320 with an always-False hook, the un-guarded version leaks a banned tree in 40/40 seeds, the shipped one in 0/40 (28 raise, 12 return the spare).
Fix: new `test_generate_fallback_never_returns_a_banned_tree_when_the_ban_covers_the_draws` — exhaustive key enumeration with `len(keys) == 320` asserted, all but one `spare` banned, `accept=lambda t: False`, 20 seeds, each outcome required to be either GenerationExhausted or exactly `{spare}` with `unaccepted_fallbacks == 1`. It also asserts both branches actually occurred (measured 13 raised / 7 spare over seeds 0..19), so it cannot silently degenerate into the vacuous shape the old test had. The single-victim case is kept as `test_generate_fallback_relaxed_tree_still_avoids_a_single_banned_key` with a docstring saying outright that nothing may rest on it.

DEFECT 2 — face mass over the full operator count (medium) — REPRODUCED, FIXED.
Reproduction: `masses = [sum(weights[face]) / len(weights[face]) ...]` does divide by the face's full membership, while Partura's pick (scripts/idea_search.py:225-238) filters `if w > 0` before grouping and therefore divides by the surviving count. Measured on the vocabulary Partura mines (`allow_resource_risk=True`, 218 specs, dt 109 / nd 46 / nt 46 / shared 17): with only `day_mean` alive in dt, shipped P(dt) = 0.0034 empirical / 0.0030 analytic against 0.2495 / 0.2500 under Partura's pick and 0.25 under the uniform path — the reported 81x, confirmed. Also confirmed nothing pinned face-balancing at all: replacing the mean with a plain sum left 27/27 green.
One number in the report did not reproduce verbatim, and it does not change the finding: the 0.1404-vs-0.2485 case ("zeroing the 55 dt/in operators") is Partura-registry-specific. AlphaCube's own registry declares only 4 resource_risk operators (nt 2 / dt 1 / shared 1), so zeroing just those shifts P(dt) 0.2548 vs 0.2500 — a real but small shift. The 55 figure must come from Partura's registry with ops_ext loaded. The mechanism, its direction and the 81x magnitude all reproduce.
Fix: weight-0 specs are dropped before the mean (`live_specs`), which makes `_pick_weighted` Partura's pick draw for draw — asserted, not inferred: new parametrised `test_pick_weighted_is_parturas_pick_draw_for_draw` compares 400 picks against a frozen local copy of that `pick` on a shared seed across five regimes (one operator boosted, a whole face banned, most of the dt face banned, mixed boosts and bans, every weight zero). Plus three tests for the two properties on their own: `test_unit_weights_leave_every_face_mass_equal` and `test_zeroing_most_of_a_face_does_not_shrink_that_faces_mass` read the masses off a recording rng, and `test_unit_weights_reproduce_the_uniform_path_face_shares` / `test_zeroing_nine_of_ten_operators_keeps_the_faces_draw_share` check the end-to-end shares through `_pick`.
Incidental finding while verifying: the shipped second draw, `choices(faces[face], weights=weights[face])`, leaves zero-weight specs in the population. That part was harmless — `random.choices` can never return a zero-weight element and the total is unchanged — but I filtered them anyway so the parity with Partura does not rest on `bisect_right` semantics.

DEFECT 3 — hook_rng is Random(0) in every mining run (medium) — REPRODUCED, FIXED (with a deviation).
Reproduction: both consequences, exactly as reported. GPMiner-style construction (`rng=random.Random(s)`, no `seed=`) gives first draws [0.844422, 0.757954, 0.420572] for s = 0, 7 and 12345 alike, while `seed=` gives three different streams; and with the default `seed=0` and no rng, hook_rng and _rng have identical first three draws, so the docstring's "second, independent stream" was false in the sense that matters. Confirmed `getstate()` does not advance the stream.
Fix: `_hook_seed` derives the hook seed from the generator stream's state (see deviations for why not `seed=seed` in gp.py). Three new tests: streams differ for rng-seeded s=7 vs s=12345 and are still deterministic; hook_rng is never _rng's sequence for all three construction styles; construction consumes no draw from a supplied rng (`probe.getstate()` unchanged — the hazard the derivation introduces); plus a SystemRandom case for the no-state fallback branch.

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY, re-verified independently of the suite: with no hooks set the generator is bit-identical to the pre-WP5 baseline tree (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube @ tradable-backtest, read-only, compared out-of-process) across 24 recorded quantities — `generate_population(60)` keys, the rng's position afterwards, 400 `_pick` names, and every mutate_subtree/mutate_operator/mutate_hoist/crossover result — for seeds 0/7/11/12345 under both `seed=` and `rng=` construction. Zero differences.

FOR WP7: nothing in WP7's step list needs to change under this fix, but its step 2 inherits a generator whose `seed` keyword is now only a fallback. If the coordinator would rather keep the design's literal hook formula, WP7 must add `seed=seed` at gp.py:241 and `_hook_seed` should be reverted; that choice is recorded in both files' docstrings.
